newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea defends nuclear waste deal with Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea defends nuclear waste deal with Taiwan.

text.p: North Korea on Monday defended its plan to accept nuclear waste from Taiwan, saying the deal would not pollute the Korean peninsula with radioactive waste.
"There is nothing whatsoever that should be seen as a problem," North Korea's official newspaper Rodong Sinmun said.
State utility Taiwan Power Co signed a contract on January 11 under which it will ship up to 200,000 barrels of nuclear waste to cash-strapped Stalinist North Korea.
Under the contract, Taipower plans to ship 60,000 barrels of waste in the first two years.
Seoul, saying that it has no verification North Korea can store the waste safely and fears nuclear contamination of the Korean peninsula, protested against the nuclear waste pact.
North Korea, however, dismissed the South's fears.
"South Korea must shut up and stop acting blindly to make a false charge against someone else," the North Korean daily said.
Taiwan has also said South Korea's concerns were unwarranted.
Taipower declined to disclose financial terms, but Taiwan media have said the utility had agreed to pay impoverished Pyongyang $1,150 for each barrel it takes.

Under a landmark $4.5 billion nuclear deal between North Korea and the United States in 1994, Pyongyang would receive two light-water reactors and interim energy supplies in exchange for the North abandoning its suspected nuclear weapons programme.
Modern light-water reactors produce little of the weapons-grade plutonium needed to make nuclear weapons.
